scope: src/main.js lines 2419-6048 — buildLevel(): level geometry, walls, regions, props, zone doors, dynamic props, verticality, lighting profiles, environment-cohesion pass.

findings.title: Environment-cohesion grade never reaches grouped signature props
findings.description: _applyCoreEnvironmentCohesionPass() iterates `ob` with `if(!mesh||!mesh.isMesh||!mesh.material)continue;`. Every signature prop is built with `new THREE.Group()` and its child meshes are attached via `grp.add(...)`, while only the Group itself is pushed to `ob` (e.g. cargoContainer 3756, hangingChain 3786, marbleCol 3833, chand 3859, fountain fGrp 3983, gurney 4029, serverRack 4252, helm 4177, sofaY 4205). A Group is an Object3D, not a Mesh, so it is skipped — none of those child meshes receive the cohesion tint/roughness/specular/envMap polish that the flat shell and floor decals get. The marquee props (the most prominent objects on screen) are exactly the ones excluded from the versioned cohesion look, so they read as un-color-graded relative to the dressed room.
findings.evidence: for(const mesh of ob){ if(!mesh||!mesh.isMesh||!mesh.material)continue; ... } — combined with `const grp=new THREE.Group();...scene.add(grp);ob.push(grp);` for every signature prop (only the group is in ob, never its meshes).
findings.fix: In _applyCoreEnvironmentCohesionPass, recurse into groups: replace the flat loop with `for(const root of ob){ root.traverse(node=>{ if(!node.isMesh||!node.material)return; ... existing per-mesh body ... }); }`. Note classify() uses `mesh.position.y` which is LOCAL inside a group — switch to a world-position lookup (`node.getWorldPosition(_tmpVec)`) for the floor/decal height tests so grouped meshes classify correctly.
findings.risk: Touching more materials per level; could shift the look of grouped props (intended). storeBase() guards against double-application so re-runs are safe. Keep the `coreVisualViewmodelPolish` skip. Verify build + probes stay green; this only mutates material params, no save/state shape.

findings.title: polishM MeshStandardMaterial built every level but only ever added for bn===1 ultra
findings.description: `polishM` is constructed unconditionally inside addCinematicRealismLayer() for every building and quality, but is only attached to the scene/ob when `bn===1 && quality==='ultra'` (line 2536). In all other cases the material is created and immediately orphaned. It is a raw `new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial`, not an _aaMat cached material, and cleanup() only disposes materials reachable through `ob`. So on every non-(B1-ultra) level load a MeshStandardMaterial (with shader program once compiled if ever) is allocated and never disposed.
findings.fix: Only build polishM inside the same guard that uses it: `let polishM=null; if(bn===1&&((SETTINGS&&SETTINGS.quality)==='ultra')){ polishM=stabilizeOverlayMaterial(new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({...}),5); addFloorOverlay(0,0,RW*.86,RD*.86,polishM,0,WT+.034); }`.
findings.risk: Trivial; pure construction-site move. No behavior change for B1-ultra. Build/probes unaffected.

findings.title: buildLevel mutates shared module textures' repeat each load
findings.description: addCinematicRealismLayer mutates the repeat of shared module-level textures: `scuffTex.repeat.set(Math.max(2,RW/12),Math.max(3,RD/12))` (scuffTex = _authoringFloorScuffMap() = shared _floorScuffTex) and `_grimeStreakTex.repeat.set(2.4,1.25)`. _grimeStreakTex is also returned by _authoringGrimeMap() and used by the grime decal material (line 2487) and grimeWallM (2521). Because UV repeat is a per-texture (not per-material) property, the last level built dictates the repeat for every reuse of that texture — including any other code paths sharing it. Loading B1 (RW=44,RD=64) vs B7 (RW=28,RD=64) leaves the scuff tiling stuck at whatever level loaded last when the texture is reused before this code re-runs.
findings.fix: Clone the texture before setting repeat (as is already done for floor maps via _cloneConcreteFloorMaps and for window slices), or accept it as cosmetic. Lowest-risk: clone scuffTex/grimeTex per material that needs a distinct repeat: `const scuffTex=_authoringFloorScuffMap().clone(); scuffTex.needsUpdate=true;` then set repeat on the clone. Dispose the clones in cleanup() (push their owning meshes — already happens) but clones aren't auto-disposed by the material .dispose(), so add them to a disposal list.
findings.risk: Cloning textures increases GPU texture count slightly. If skipped, only a subtle tiling-scale inconsistency. Keep probes green.

findings.title: visualStats.dressingObjects double-counts B1 pallets
findings.description: Inside addAAVisualDressing the B1 pallet loop does `visualStats.dressingObjects+=9` (line 2642). At the end of the function `visualStats.dressingObjects+=ob.length-startCount` (line 2702) adds the total number of meshes pushed during the function — which already includes those 9 pallet meshes. So for bn===1 the dressingObjects telemetry is inflated by 9. Diagnostic-only (visualStats), no gameplay effect, but the number is wrong and could mislead any perf/density tuning that reads it.
findings.fix: Remove the redundant `visualStats.dressingObjects+=9;` on line 2642 (the catch-all at 2702 already counts those meshes), or zero startCount handling. Simplest: delete line 2642.
findings.risk: None — pure stat correction. Verify no probe asserts an exact dressingObjects value for B1.

findings.title: Nightclub disco flare meshes tagged discoFlareVisual but never animated
findings.description: For bn===3 four corner glow spheres are created and tagged `flare.userData.discoFlareVisual=true`, and the matching fake lamp gets `userData:{baseIntensity:1.2,discoFlare:true}`. Neither flag is read anywhere in the codebase (grep: discoFlareVisual / discoFlare have no consumers). The disco ball itself rotates and hue-cycles via dynProps 'disco', but these four side flares are static, non-pulsing additive spheres. In a nightclub the most expected motion is pulsing/strobing accent lights, so this is a half-wired feature: the intent (animated flares) was tagged but the tick was never written.
findings.evidence: fakeCeilingLamps.push({...userData:{baseIntensity:1.2,discoFlare:true}}); ... flare.userData.discoFlareVisual=true; — no reader exists for either flag.
findings.fix: In tickDynProps (or the lighting tick) pulse these: register them like other dynProps, e.g. push `dynProps.push({type:'discoFlare',grp:flare,phaseX:Math.random()*6.28})` and add a branch: `else if(dp.type==='discoFlare'){ dp.grp.material.opacity=.30+0.35*Math.abs(Math.sin(now*3.4+dp.phaseX)); dp.grp.material.color.setHSL((now*.5+dp.phaseX)%1,.95,.55); }`. Cheap, high on-screen payoff for the club level.
findings.risk: Adds a few per-frame opacity/color writes for B3 only. Material.opacity already transparent. No state/save impact.

findings.title: Cabinet drawer-pull loop comment says three, loop runs once
findings.description: cabinet() comment reads 'Drawer pulls — three horizontal bumps' but the loop is `for(let i=0;i<1;i++)`, so exactly one pull row is drawn. The `i*.32` y-offset term is therefore always 0 and is dead. Either the loop bound was reduced (perf) and the comment/offset left stale, or it was meant to be 3. Visually the cabinets look bare vs the authored intent.
findings.evidence:
// Drawer pulls — three horizontal bumps
    for(let i=0;i<1;i++){ box(x,WT+0.30+i*.32,z+(rotY?0:d/2-.01), .12,.04,.02, cabinetHdlM); ... }
findings.fix: Decide intent: if three pulls are wanted, change to `for(let i=0;i<3;i++)` (the i*.32 offset then becomes live and the cabinets gain detail); if one is intended for perf, drop the loop and the stale comment. Recommend i<3 for the cheap visual gain.
findings.risk: i<3 adds 4 tiny boxes per cabinet × 4 cabinets per non-B1 level. Negligible. Confirm no probe counts cabinet meshes.

findings.title: addWindow computes unused `inset` variable
findings.description: `const fT=.04,inset=faceDir.includes('x')?.0:.0;` — `inset` is always 0 (both branches .0) and is never referenced after declaration. Dead code / leftover of an abandoned inset attempt.

findings.title: Dead legacy B01 block redeclares fM, shadowing the level floor material name
findings.description: Inside the `if(bn===1&&legacyB01ProceduralDressing)` block (legacyB01ProceduralDressing is hard-coded false at line 2425, so the whole block is unreachable) there is `const fM=new THREE.MeshPhongMaterial({color:0xd0a020,...})` for the forklift, reusing the same identifier as the level floor material `const fM=_aaMat(floorKind,...)` declared at line 2779. The forklift fM is block-scoped so it does not corrupt the outer fM, but this is dead code (gated false) plus a confusing name collision. The whole legacy block (3750-3826) and the matching Sifu/debris legacy blocks (3336-3420 partly, 3907-3920) can never execute.
findings.fix: Either delete the legacyB01ProceduralDressing-gated dead branches entirely (they are confirmed unreachable and B1 now uses applySequenceLayout + per-building verticality), or if kept for reference, rename the inner forklift material (e.g. fLiftM) to avoid the fM collision. Lower risk: leave behavior, just remove the dead branches to cut ~120 lines of confusion.
findings.risk: Deleting dead code: confirm no other code references symbols defined only inside those blocks (none escape — all local). Build/probes unaffected since the branch never ran.

findings.title: Cohesion classify() uses local mesh.position.y for floor/decal height tests
findings.description: classify() decides decal/wet/prop role partly via `mesh.position.y<=WT+.075` and `mesh.position.y<=WT+.08 && (gp.height||0)<=.025`. For any mesh whose position is relative to a parent (would matter once the grouped-prop traversal in env-cohesion-skips-grouped-props is fixed, and also already matters for the floor-overlay meshes added via addFloorOverlay which set y on the mesh directly — those are fine since top-level). The latent bug surfaces the moment grouped meshes are included: a sheet mesh at local y=0.013 inside a group sitting at world y=2.4 (mezzanine) would be wrongly classified as a floor decal and get polygonOffset/renderOrder 4 + noReflect.
findings.fix: Use world Y: at top of classify resolve `const wy = mesh.parent && mesh.parent!==scene ? mesh.getWorldPosition(_tmpV).y : mesh.position.y;` (reuse a module scratch Vector3) and test against `wy`. Pair this with the grouped-prop traversal fix.
findings.risk: Adds a getWorldPosition per classified mesh (cheap, one-time at level build). Must ensure world matrices are current — call scene.updateMatrixWorld(true) once before the cohesion pass if not already updated.

findings.title: Animated CRT monitor material exists but only 2-3 wall monitors use it
findings.description: monitorScreenM (line 3508) is a live emissive-map CRT screen driven by _drawMonitorCanvas every 3rd frame (43945) — a genuinely AAA animated-screen asset. But buildLevel only places 2 generic wallMonitor calls (plus one for bn>=2), and all the per-building screens (B5 vital monitors line 4090, B6 ticket/map screens, B8 terminal monitors 4294/4845, helm displays 4183) use flat static MeshBasicMaterial cyan/black quads instead of the animated monitorScreenM. The expensive animated-screen feature is under-used, so most 'screens' in the game are dead flat color while the system to make them live already runs each frame.
findings.evidence: wallMonitor uses monitorScreenM, but e.g. B8 terminal: `const monM=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color:0x40c8ff});` (line 4294); B5 vitals: `new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color:0x040608})` (4090); helm: `new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color:0x40c8ff})` (4183).
findings.fix: Swap a handful of the most player-facing static screen MeshBasicMaterials to share monitorScreenM (the emissiveMap texture is shared so cost is one canvas redraw, already happening). At minimum: B8 terminal monitors (4294), B5 reception monitor (4708), helm display panels (4183). Reuse the single monitorScreenM instance (do NOT clone — it shares _monitorTex). Instant 'screens are alive' upgrade with near-zero added cost.
findings.risk: monitorScreenM is MeshPhongMaterial; replacing MeshBasicMaterial planes changes lighting response (screens become slightly lit). Verify they still read as bright (emissiveIntensity 1.10 keeps them glowing). Shared material so no extra disposal. Don't apply to planes that need exact alignment as bezels.

findings.title: Faked god-ray cones only render on low/medium; high/ultra get nothing unless Phase2 volumetrics shipped
findings.description: useConeGodrays is set to `!cinemaRayQ` where cinemaRayQ is true for high/ultra. The comment says high+ should instead get the Phase 2 volumetric post pass. If a player runs on high/ultra but Phase 2 volumetrics is disabled/absent (SETTINGS.phase2Volumetrics not true), the result is NO light-shaft volumetrics at all under the ceiling lamps — high/ultra can look flatter than medium for that one effect. Low/medium get the cheap cone shafts; high/ultra fall through to (possibly absent) post FX.
findings.evidence: let useConeGodrays=!cinemaRayQ; try{ if(SETTINGS.phase2Volumetrics===false)useConeGodrays=false; }catch(_){}  — for high/ultra cinemaRayQ is true so useConeGodrays starts false; only the explicit ===false re-confirms off, never turns the cones back on.
findings.fix: If the Phase 2 volumetric post pass is not actually active, keep the cheap cones on for high/ultra too: `let useConeGodrays=!cinemaRayQ || !(SETTINGS && SETTINGS.phase2Volumetrics===true);` so high/ultra without the post pass still get shafts. Verify the post-pass path actually runs before relying on it (check _renderStack for a volumetric pass) to avoid double shafts.
findings.risk: Could double-render shafts if Phase 2 volumetrics IS active — gate carefully on the same flag the post pass reads. The cone material opacity is .012 so even if both ran the artifact is faint. Validate visually per quality tier.

findings.title: Cover-scatter set and mood-light color tables only defined for buildings 1-8
findings.description: _coverSets only has keys 1..8 and falls back to _coverSets[1] (wooden crates) for bn 9-12 via `const cset=_coverSets[bn]||_coverSets[1];`. Likewise moodCol map `({1:..,..,8:..})[bn]||0xffd060` falls back to amber. So Act III buildings (9 Border, 10 Cathedral, 11 Freighter, 12 Spire) scatter wooden crates (cset name 'crate') and amber mood dots regardless of theme — a cathedral and a chrome spire both get warehouse crates as procedural cover. This reads as a half-finished extension when Act III was added (BUILDING_DIMS/pal/lightProfile/_texProfile all go to 12, but cover/mood tables stopped at 8).
findings.fix: Add entries 9-12 to _coverSets (e.g. 9 sandbag/crate desert, 10 'pedestal'/'plinth' marble, 11 'rack'/'crate' steel, 12 'pillar' chrome) and to moodCol (9 0xffb060, 10 0xffe8b0, 11 0x80b0d0, 12 0xc8e0ff to match accentColors). Low effort, removes the warehouse-crate-in-a-cathedral incongruity.
findings.risk: applySequenceLayout already provides the primary themed props for 9-12, so this scatter is supplementary; ensure new cover doesn't collide with sequence cells. Confirm probes don't assert cset for bn>8.

findings.title: Cathedral choir-loft candles are bare emissive cylinders with no pool/glow lamp
findings.description: B10 choir loft places four candle meshes as plain MeshBasicMaterial cylinders (color 0xffe8b0) with no accompanying fakeCeilingLamps pool entry and no flicker. Other set-piece lights in the function (chandelier 3853, disco 3906, fountain 3990, fireplace 4002) all call _aaPushFakePoolLamp so the lighting controller tints nearby surfaces. The cathedral's signature votive candles contribute zero light interaction and don't flicker — they look like glowing toothpicks rather than candlelight in the level whose whole identity is 'votive candle pools in deep gothic shadow' (lightProfile comment line 3112).
findings.evidence: const candle=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.06,0.08,0.30,8),new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({color:0xffe8b0})); candle.position.set(cx,chY+0.40,-22); scene.add(candle);ob.push(candle); — no _aaPushFakePoolLamp, no dynProps flicker.
findings.fix: For each candle add a small additive glow sphere + a fake pool lamp: `_aaPushFakePoolLamp(fakeCeilingLamps,cx,chY+0.55,-22,0xffd090,1.2,{candle:true});` and optionally register a subtle flicker (reuse the L.userData.flicker path or a dynProps 'fire'-style scale jitter on a small flame plane). High atmospheric payoff for the cathedral.
findings.risk: Adds 4 fake lamps to B10 (fake lamps are budget-free meshes, not PointLights). Keep additive glow opacity low to avoid bloom blowout. No state impact.
